scope: Theorem 4.2 (Uniform weight denominator) of the manuscript “Uniform log Iitaka fibrations and bounded moduli denominators” (preprints/Uniform-log-Iitaka-fibrations-and-bounded-moduli-denominators-October-4-2026/uniform-log-iitaka.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 034 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0fee79cbeaa3ae4f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 7-8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For integers s ≥ 0 and m ≥ 1 there is an integer q(s, m) > 0 with the following property. Let C be a smooth projective complex curve, c ∈ C, and z a rational uniformizer at c. Let V be a normal geometrically integral projective 7 s-fold over K = C(C), and let (V, B) be a geometrically log canonical pair with effective rational boundary. If a rational relative m-canonical form ϕ satisfies divV (ϕ) + mB = 0, (4.2) then q(s, m)wz(ϕ) ∈ Z. The integer q(s, m) is independent of the boundary coefficients and of the curve, variety, and form.
